A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conformal-mask framework for image super-resolution. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v1 Appendix A and v2 Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original SinSR experiments on Liu4K, including fidelity-error curves, mask-size and blur analyses, and qualitative reconstruction examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original quantitative results in Table 1, PSNR and simulated data-leakage experiments in Figure 4, baseline comparisons, and colorization examples in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The calibration equations, variance-based scores, smoothing components, and fidelity-function choices are retained. Appendix C documents algorithms already described in v1; the colorization application does not establish a new calibration procedure or method component.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds an actual image-colorization task using DDColor, illustrated with six grayscale-to-color examples. v1 evaluated super-resolution and only mentioned colorization as a possible application. The Liu4K super-resolution coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds evaluated outputs from Angelopoulos et al. (2022b) and Kutiel et al. (2023). These methods were cited but not shown in corresponding comparisons in v1. The no-uncertainty baseline is retained; the added prior-method comparisons are qualitative.

E3.justification: v2 introduces empirical evaluation of PSNR within trusted regions against whole-image reconstruction, and a leakage protocol that recalibrates after assigning zero fidelity error to varying numbers of calibration samples. These protocols were absent from v1, which presented the corresponding theoretical bounds.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds empirical checks of PSNR-bound tightness and robustness to simulated calibration leakage. Figure 2 expands semantic versus non-semantic mask analyses. Existing blur and failure-case analyses are also reworked: v1 Figure 7 maps to the expanded v2 Figure 5, and the principal close-up case is retained.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 5 explicitly identifies its bands as 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals. v2 retains shaded bands and adds Table 1's ± values without defining their uncertainty statistic or confidence level. This changes uncertainty documentation but does not establish changed run counts or estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including Table 1, leakage curves, prior-method outputs, and colorization examples. At α = 0.100, Table 1 newly reports trusted-region PSNR means of 32.65 and 28.64 for semantic and non-semantic calibration, respectively. These are newly reported evaluations, not demonstrated performance gains over matching v1 results.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a formal risk-guarantee statement, analysis of the calibration procedure attributed to Kutiel et al. (2023), and counterexample B.1 challenging that guarantee. The original three guarantees and Appendix A proofs are retained. Making the PSNR logarithm explicitly base 10 matches the existing v1 proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain model-agnostic confidence masks, fidelity and PSNR guarantees, leakage robustness, and benefits from smoothing. v2 foregrounds broader restoration applicability, but v1 already claimed applicability to inpainting and colorization; the new examples support that retained claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about the PSNR bound becoming loose at higher α and the leakage bound being tighter under limited contamination. It also adds interpretations of why binary masks convey uncertainty more directly than the displayed interval-valued and continuous-score baseline outputs.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly supplies dynamic-programming and brute-force calibration pseudocode. Section 4 newly assigns training data to calibration and test data to evaluation, without establishing a changed split. Reported hardware changes from AMD EPYC/A100 with 216GB RAM to Intel Xeon/RTX 6000 Ada with 40GB RAM. Both versions retain the redacted code-URL placeholder.

R1.justification: The existing related-work coverage and central positioning are retained. v2 adds the DDColor citation, clarifies the distinction between Kutiel's continuous scores and its own binary masks, and develops a focused critique in Appendix B supporting the previously asserted distinction in guarantees.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Conformal' to 'Conformalized,' and the author block, captions, and experimental narrative are edited. Section 4 replaces Resources/Results subsections with descriptive paragraph headings. Most introduction, method, theory, and original proof prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout and extensively reorganizes its displays, including combined qualitative comparisons, a three-panel Figure 2, new Table 1, and new PSNR, leakage, baseline, and colorization figures. v2 Figure 2's caption incorrectly swaps the semantic/non-semantic mask-size panels and misidentifies the semantic curve's color.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the retained PSNR and leakage claims through Table 1 and Figure 4, and makes prior-method outputs and calibration procedures more inspectable through Figure 6 and Appendix C. However, the added baseline and colorization evidence is qualitative, Figure 2 introduces misleading panel descriptions, and uncertainty reporting loses explicit definitions. The net improvement in evidence and transparency is positive but limited by these reporting defects.
